notes:
Thank you for reviewing Tipsaver.

WHAT THE APP DOES
Tipsaver is a tip tracker for people who work for tips (servers, baristas, delivery drivers, stylists). The user logs each shift (card tips, cash tips, hours) and sees totals, hourly pay and a shareable "slip" (a picture of the shift in the shape of a receipt).

NO ACCOUNT
There is no sign-in and no account. All data is stored on the device. No demo account is needed.

HOW TO TRY IT QUICKLY
1. Open the app and go through the two setup screens (any answers). "Log my first shift" opens the shift form.
2. Type an amount with the keypad and tap "Save shift". The slip appears. Close it with the X.
3. The subscription screen: gear button at the top right of Home → Tipsaver Pro. "Not now", at the top right of that screen, closes it.

SUBSCRIPTION (Tipsaver Pro)
- Auto-renewable subscription, monthly or yearly (yearly includes a 1-week free trial).
- The subscription screen opens from Settings → Tipsaver Pro, from locked features (the charts of the Insights tab other than "Best days", tax estimate and PDF on the Taxes tab, week/month/year slips, slip styles, second job), and once by itself when the slip of the third logged shift is closed.
- It shows the title, the length and the price of each plan, states that the plan renews automatically, and links to the Terms of Use (Apple's standard EULA) and to the Privacy Policy. "Restore purchases" is on the same screen and in Settings.
- Free features: unlimited shift logging, totals, history, weekly goal, best days of the week, one job, shift slips, CSV export and import, reminders. The subscription screen says so at the top ("Everything you use today stays free.").

TAX INFORMATION (UNITED STATES ONLY)
With Country set to United States (Settings → Country; it follows the device region at first launch), the fourth tab is "Taxes". It shows how much of the logged tips may count toward the U.S. federal deduction for qualified tips (tax years 2025–2028) and, for subscribers, an estimate of the federal income tax saved. Figures come from IRS publications. The screen states that these are estimates and not tax advice, and refers users to a tax professional or IRS.gov. In other countries the tab is "Year" (a summary of the year) and the subscription screen does not mention taxes.

NOTIFICATIONS
Only local notifications: an optional reminder to log a shift, at a time chosen by the user, and an optional weekly recap. The permission is never asked at launch: it is asked when the user taps "Turn on reminders" on a card shown on Home after the first shift, or turns a switch on in Settings → Reminders. No remote push notifications are sent.

DATA
No advertising, no tracking, no in-app behavioural analytics. Purchases are validated with RevenueCat, which receives the purchase history under an anonymous identifier and gives us aggregate subscription statistics. This is declared in App Privacy as Purchases → Purchase History (App Functionality, Analytics), not linked to the user's identity and not used for tracking.
